name: Time, Work, Pipes & Cisterns
intro: **Assume the total work is the LCM of the given times.** Every rate then becomes a whole number and the fractions disappear from the entire solution (§1).
A pipe that empties is a negative rate. Nothing else about §7 differs from ordinary work problems.

qs.q: A can do a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, how many days do they take?
qs.h: §1 — take the total work as LCM(12, 18) = 36 units.
qs.s: Rates 3 and 2 units/day ⟹ 5 together ⟹ 36/5 = 7.2 days.

qs.q: A and B together do a job in 8 days; A alone takes 12 days. B alone takes
qs.h: §1 — LCM(8, 12) = 24. Subtract rates, never times.
qs.s: Total 24 units: together 3/day, A 2/day ⟹ B = 1/day ⟹ 24 days. (Subtracting 12 from 8 is meaningless — rates subtract, times don't.)

qs.q: A is twice as efficient as B, and together they finish a job in 12 days. How many days does A alone take?
qs.h: §2 — efficiency ratio 2 : 1 means the combined rate is 3 parts, of which A supplies 2.
qs.s: Combined = 3 parts in 12 days ⟹ A's 2 parts take 12 × 3/2 = 18 days (B takes 36).

qs.q: A, B and C can do a job in 10, 12 and 15 days respectively. Working together they take
qs.s: Rates 6, 5 and 4 ⟹ 15/day ⟹ 60/15 = 4 days.

qs.q: A can do a job in 20 days and B in 30 days. They work together for 6 days, then A leaves. How many more days does B need?
qs.h: §11 — count the units done, then divide the remainder by B's rate alone.
qs.s: Total 60 units, rates 3 and 2. Six days together = 30 units ⟹ 30 remain ⟹ B needs 30/2 = 15 days.

qs.q: If 3 men can do a piece of work in 8 days, then 4 men take
qs.h: §3 — total man-days is fixed. More men means fewer days: an inverse proportion.

sets.name: Men, days and hours (the M-D-H formula)

qs.q: If 12 men working 8 hours a day complete a job in 15 days, how many days will 20 men working 9 hours a day take?
qs.h: §3 — men × days × hours is a constant for a fixed job.

qs.q: 15 workers build a wall in 48 days. The number of workers needed to build it in 30 days is
qs.h: §3 — men and days are inversely proportional.
qs.s: 15 × 48 = 720 worker-days ⟹ 720/30 = 24 workers.

qs.q: 6 men and 8 boys can do a job in 10 days, while 26 men and 48 boys can do it in 2 days. How many days would 15 men and 20 boys take?
qs.h: §10 — let m and b be the daily rates of one man and one boy, form two equations and eliminate.

qs.q: If 8 machines running 6 hours a day produce 480 units in 5 days, then 12 machines running 8 hours a day produce, in 3 days,
qs.h: §3 — find the output per machine-hour, then scale up. Output is directly proportional here, not inversely.
qs.s: 480/(8 × 6 × 5) = 2 units per machine-hour ⟹ 12 × 8 × 3 × 2 = 576 units.

qs.q: 10 men can complete a work in 12 days. After 4 days, 5 more men join. In how many more days is the work finished? Give the answer to two decimals.
qs.h: §5 — convert to man-days, subtract what's done, divide by the new workforce.
qs.s: Total 120 man-days; 40 done ⟹ 80 remain with 15 men ⟹ 80/15 = 5.33 days.

qs.q: A can do a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. They work on alternate days starting with A. How many days does the job take?
qs.h: §4 — find the work done per 2-day cycle, run whole cycles, then finish day by day.
qs.s: Total 30 units; A 3/day, B 2/day ⟹ 5 per cycle. Five cycles (10 days) = 25 units. Day 11: A adds 3 ⟹ 28. Day 12: B adds 2 ⟹ 30 ⟹ 12 days.

qs.q: A can do a job in 12 days and B in 24 days. Working on alternate days starting with B, the job takes
qs.h: §4 — who starts changes the cycle order but not its total. Check whether the job ends exactly on a cycle boundary.
qs.s: Total 24 units; A 2, B 1 ⟹ 3 per cycle. Eight cycles = 16 days and exactly 24 units ⟹ 16 days.

qs.q: A, B and C can do a job in 6, 12 and 24 days. They work in rotation, one day each, starting with A. How many days does the job take?
qs.h: §4 — three-day cycle. When the last cycle overshoots, take the fractional part of that worker's day.
qs.s: Total 24 units; rates 4, 2, 1 ⟹ 7 per 3-day cycle. Three cycles (9 days) = 21 units ⟹ 3 remain and A does 4/day ⟹ ¾ of a day ⟹ 9.75 days.

qs.q: A does a job in 9 days and B in 18 days. Working alternately starting with A, the work is completed in
qs.h: §4 — check whether the cycles land exactly on the total.
qs.s: Total 18 units; A 2, B 1 ⟹ 3 per cycle. Six cycles = 12 days and exactly 18 units ⟹ 12 days.

qs.q: Two taps fill a tank in 20 and 30 minutes. They are opened alternately for one minute each, starting with the first. How many minutes does the tank take to fill?
qs.h: §4 + §7 — identical machinery, minutes instead of days.
qs.s: Total 60 units; rates 3 and 2 ⟹ 5 per 2-minute cycle. Eleven cycles (22 min) = 55 units. Minute 23: +3 ⟹ 58. Minute 24: +2 ⟹ 60 ⟹ 24 minutes.

qs.q: A can do a job in 15 days and B in 20 days. They start together but A leaves after 4 days. In how many more days does B finish? Give the answer to two decimals.
qs.h: §5 — units done, then remainder over B's rate.
qs.s: Total 60 units; rates 4 and 3. Four days together = 28 ⟹ 32 remain ⟹ 32/3 = 10.67 days.

qs.q: A and B together do a job in 12 days. They work for 8 days, then A leaves and B finishes the rest in 6 days. B alone would take
qs.h: §11 — the fraction B does alone, divided by the time it took, gives B's rate.
qs.s: In 8 days they finish 8/12 = 2/3 ⟹ B does the remaining 1/3 in 6 days ⟹ B alone takes 18 days.

qs.q: A can do a job in 24 days. He works for 6 days, then B finishes the remaining work in 9 days. How many days would B alone take for the whole job?
qs.h: §11 — find the fraction left, then scale B's 9 days up to the whole job.
qs.s: A does 6/24 = 1/4 ⟹ 3/4 remains, done by B in 9 days ⟹ B alone takes 9 ÷ 3/4 = 12 days.

qs.q: 20 men start a job scheduled to take 30 days. After 10 days, 5 men leave. The total time taken is
qs.h: §5 — work in man-days throughout, and remember to add back the 10 days already spent.
qs.s: Total 600 man-days; 200 done ⟹ 400 remain with 15 men ⟹ 26.67 more days ⟹ 36.67 days in total.

qs.q: A, B and C together do a job in 8 days. A alone takes 24 days and B alone 32 days. How many days does C alone take?
qs.h: §1 — take LCM(8, 24, 32) = 96 and subtract rates.
qs.s: Total 96 units: together 12/day, A 4, B 3 ⟹ C = 5/day ⟹ 96/5 = 19.2 days.

qs.q: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours and another empties it in 9 hours. With both open, how many hours does the tank take to fill?
qs.h: §7 — the emptying pipe is a negative rate. Take LCM(6, 9) = 18.
qs.s: Rates +3 and −2 ⟹ net 1 unit/hour ⟹ 18 hours.

qs.q: Two pipes fill a tank in 12 and 15 minutes; a waste pipe empties it in 20 minutes. With all three open, the tank fills in
qs.h: §7 — LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60; add the fillers and subtract the drain.
qs.s: Rates +5, +4, −3 ⟹ net 6/min ⟹ 60/6 = 10 minutes.

qs.q: A tank is filled by pipe A in 20 minutes and by pipe B in 30 minutes. Both are opened, but A is closed after 5 minutes. How many more minutes does B need?
qs.h: §7 + §5 — the same leave-midway structure as D1.
qs.s: Total 60 units; rates 3 and 2. Five minutes together = 25 ⟹ 35 remain ⟹ 35/2 = 17.5 minutes.

qs.q: A leak empties a full cistern in 8 hours. With a tap admitting 6 litres a minute turned on, the cistern empties in 12 hours instead. Its capacity is
qs.h: §7 — the tap's rate is the difference of the two emptying rates. Convert litres per minute to litres per hour at the end.
qs.s: Tap rate = 1/8 − 1/12 = 1/24 of the tank per hour ⟹ the tap alone would fill it in 24 hours at 360 litres/hour ⟹ capacity = 8,640 litres.

qs.q: Two pipes fill a tank in 15 and 20 hours. Both are opened together, but the first is closed after 4 hours. In how many more hours is the tank full? Give the answer to two decimals.
qs.s: Rates 4 and 3. Four hours together = 28 units ⟹ 32 remain ⟹ 32/3 = 10.67 hours.

qs.q: A and B can do a job in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 20 days. How many days would all three together take?
qs.h: §9 — add all three pairwise rates; the sum counts each worker twice.
qs.s: Total 60 units: A+B = 5, B+C = 4, C+A = 3 ⟹ 2(A+B+C) = 12 ⟹ 6/day ⟹ 10 days.

qs.q: A and B can do a job in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 20 days. A alone would take
qs.h: §9 — get the three-person rate first, then subtract the pair that excludes A.
qs.s: A+B+C = 6 units/day and B+C = 4 ⟹ A = 2/day ⟹ 60/2 = 30 days.

qs.q: A and B take on a job for ₹3,200. A alone can do it in 12 days and B in 16 days. With C's help they finish in 6 days. Find C's share (in ₹).
qs.h: §6 — wages split in the ratio of work done, which is the ratio of rates when all work the same number of days.
qs.s: Total 48 units: A 4, B 3, all three 8 ⟹ C = 1/day. Ratio 4 : 3 : 1 ⟹ C gets 3200/8 = ₹400.

qs.q: A does 3/5 of a job in 9 days. He then calls B, and together they finish the rest in 4 days. B alone would take
qs.h: §8 — convert each statement into a rate, then subtract A's rate from the combined rate.
qs.s: A's rate = (3/5)/9 = 1/15. Remaining 2/5 in 4 days ⟹ combined = 1/10 ⟹ B = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30 ⟹ 30 days.

qs.q: A is 60% more efficient than B. If B alone takes 40 days, how many days do they take together? Give the answer to two decimals.
qs.h: §2 — "60% more efficient" scales the rate, not the time. A's rate is 1.6 times B's.
qs.s: B = 1/40, A = 1.6/40 = 1/25 ⟹ combined = 13/200 ⟹ 200/13 = 15.38 days. (A alone takes 25 days, not 40/1.6 rounded carelessly.)

qs.q: A can do a job in 16 days and B in 24 days. Working together, how many days do they take?
qs.s: Rates 3 and 2 ⟹ 5/day ⟹ 48/5 = 9.6 days.

qs.q: If 18 men can build a wall in 20 days, then 24 men can build it in
qs.h: Man-days are fixed.

qs.q: A pipe fills a tank in 10 hours while a leak empties the full tank in 15 hours. With both operating, how many hours does the tank take to fill?
qs.h: Net rate on a base of LCM(10, 15) = 30.
qs.s: +3 and −2 ⟹ net 1/hour ⟹ 30 hours.

qs.q: A and B can complete a job in 10 days, B and C in 12 days, and A and C in 15 days. B alone would take
qs.h: Sum the pairs, halve, then subtract the pair that excludes B.

qs.q: A does a job in 18 days and B in 12 days. Working alternately starting with B, how many days does the job take? Give the answer to two decimals.
qs.h: Cycle first, then finish the fractional day.
qs.s: Total 36 units; A 2, B 3 ⟹ 5 per cycle. Seven cycles (14 days) = 35 ⟹ 1 unit remains and B does 3/day ⟹ ⅓ day ⟹ 14.33 days.

qs.q: 4 men and 6 women complete a job in 8 days, while 3 men and 7 women complete it in 10 days. The number of days 10 women take is
qs.h: Two equations in the individual rates; eliminate the men.
qs.s: 32m + 48w = 1 and 30m + 70w = 1 ⟹ w = 1/400 ⟹ 10 women work at 1/40 per day ⟹ 40 days.

qs.q: A cistern is filled by two pipes in 12 and 16 minutes. Both are opened together; after how many minutes should the first be closed so that the tank is exactly full in 10 minutes?
qs.h: The second pipe runs the whole 10 minutes; solve for the first pipe's running time.

qs.q: A, B and C earn ₹5,400 for a job in which A and B together do 7/12 of the work. C's share is
qs.h: Wages follow the fraction of work done.

qs.q: A is thrice as good a workman as B, and together they finish a job in 15 days. How many days does B alone take?
qs.h: Rates in the ratio 3 : 1, so the combined rate is 4 parts.
qs.s: 4 parts take 15 days ⟹ B's 1 part takes 60 days (A takes 20).

qs.q: 12 men complete 2/5 of a job in 8 days. The number of additional men needed to finish the rest in 6 days is
qs.h: Scale to the whole job in man-days, then answer the question actually asked.
qs.s: 96 man-days for 2/5 ⟹ 240 for the whole ⟹ 144 remain in 6 days ⟹ 24 men needed ⟹ 12 additional men. (24 is the total, planted as an option elsewhere in this style.)

audit: subtracting times instead of rates — only rates add and subtract (§1, §9)
applying an efficiency ratio to the times rather than to the rates (§2)
losing track of man-days, or forgetting to add the days already elapsed (§3, §5)
B3, M6
trying to solve two-worker-type problems with one variable
running whole cycles past the finish instead of stopping at the fractional day (§4)
C2, C4
assuming a fractional day is always needed — sometimes the cycles land exactly
using the elapsed time as a rate instead of converting the fraction of work done (§8, §11)
adding the emptying pipe instead of subtracting it (§7)
E4
forgetting to convert litres per minute into the same time unit as the rest of the problem
F3, M8
splitting wages equally or by days worked instead of by work done (§6)
M7
assuming both pipes run for the same time
reporting the total workforce where the question asked for the additional men
